# plotsizing

plotsizing estimates the size and shape of the experimental unit (plot)
from agricultural uniformity trials. It fits a bivariate surface to the
coefficient of variation (CV) of all plot configurations that can be
formed from the trial, and derives plot width and length jointly from
that surface.

Packages such as `agricolae`, `optsize` and `trialSizing` estimate plot
size from the one-dimensional relation between CV and plot area, and
choose the shape afterwards. plotsizing works on the two-dimensional
surface instead, so size and shape come out of the same calculation.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jcrodriguez1989/plotsizing")
```

## Example

The package includes four uniformity trials from Guanacaste, Costa Rica:
rice and maize (20 x 20 basic units) and Nambí common bean and cowpea
(10 x 20 basic units).

``` r

library(plotsizing)

trial <- example_trial("rice")
result <- analyze_uniformity_trial(trial, criterion = "all")

result            # trial, Smith index, fitted surface and solutions
summary(result)   # adds descriptive statistics and standard errors
plot(result)      # CV contours with the three solutions
```

The vignette walks through a complete analysis:
[`vignette("plotsizing")`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/articles/plotsizing.md).

To analyse your own trial, save the yields as a CSV with one column per
field column, a header row and no row-number column:

``` csv
C1,C2,C3,C4
390,404,308,354
460,310,362,400
320,474,424,452
```

``` r

trial <- read_trial_matrix("my_trial.csv")
result <- analyze_uniformity_trial(trial, unit_width_m = 1, unit_length_m = 1,
                                   criterion = "all")
```

`unit_width_m` and `unit_length_m` give the physical size of one basic
unit and are only used to convert the results to metres.

## Methods

The CV surface

``` math
CV(x, y) = a\, x^{-m} y^{-n}
```

is fitted by nonlinear least squares, with `x` the plot width and `y`
the plot length in basic units, and CV in percent. Three criteria are
available, each with a closed-form solution:

- `"gaussian"`: the point of maximum Gaussian curvature of the surface.
- `"sectional"`: the point where the CV curves along width and along
  length both reach their maximum curvature, the two-dimensional version
  of the modified maximum-curvature method.
- `"marginal"`: the point where the CV decreases by `target_slope`
  percentage points per additional basic unit, both along width and
  along length.

The package also fits the Smith (1938) variance law by weighted least
squares (weights `M - 1`, free intercept) and enumerates every exact
rectangular partition of the trial with at least two plots.

All calculations use basic-unit coordinates and CV in percent. The
results depend on that choice of scale, and on `target_slope` for the
marginal criterion, so the continuous solutions should be compared with
the plot configurations that are feasible in the field.

## Plots

`plot(result, which = ...)` draws `"contours"`, `"surface"`,
`"sections"`, `"profiles"` or `"heatmap"`. The underlying functions can
also be called directly:

``` r

cfg <- result$configurations
surface <- result$surface

plot_trial_heatmap(trial)
plot_cv_profiles(cfg, surface)
plot_cv_contours(surface, cfg)
plot_cv_surface(surface, cfg)
plot_curvature_sections(surface, criterion = "all", configurations = cfg)
plot_multicrop_curvature()
```

## Citation

``` r

citation("plotsizing")
```

The package was previously developed under the name `curvaUE`.

# Package index

## Complete analysis

- [`analyze_uniformity_trial()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/analyze_uniformity_trial.md)
  : Analyze an experimental uniformity trial
- [`print(`*`<plotsizing_analysis>`*`)`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/print.plotsizing_analysis.md)
  : Print a uniformity-trial analysis
- [`summary(`*`<plotsizing_analysis>`*`)`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/summary.plotsizing_analysis.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.plotsizing_analysis>`*`)`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/summary.plotsizing_analysis.md)
  : Summarize a uniformity-trial analysis
- [`plot(`*`<plotsizing_analysis>`*`)`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/plot.plotsizing_analysis.md)
  : Plot a uniformity-trial analysis

## Trial data

- [`read_trial_matrix()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/read_trial_matrix.md)
  : Read an experimental yield grid from CSV or Windows clipboard
- [`example_trial()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/example_trial.md)
  : Load one of four example uniformity trials
- [`describe_trial()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/describe_trial.md)
  : Describe a uniformity trial
- [`as_long_trial_data()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/as_long_trial_data.md)
  : Convert a spatial grid into long-format observations

## Configurations and fitted models

- [`trial_configurations()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/trial_configurations.md)
  : Enumerate admissible experimental-unit geometries
- [`fit_smith()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/fit_smith.md)
  : Estimate Smith heterogeneity using weighted log variance
- [`fit_cv_surface()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/fit_cv_surface.md)
  : Fit a bivariate power-law CV surface

## Criteria

- [`max_gaussian_curvature()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/max_gaussian_curvature.md)
  : Maximum Gaussian curvature solution
- [`simultaneous_sectional_curvature()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/simultaneous_sectional_curvature.md)
  : Simultaneous sectional curvature solution
- [`marginal_efficiency_2d()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/marginal_efficiency_2d.md)
  : Experimental-unit dimensions by two-dimensional marginal efficiency
- [`gaussian_curvature_at()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/gaussian_curvature_at.md)
  : Gaussian curvature at a point

## Plots

- [`plot_curvature_sections()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/plot_curvature_sections.md)
  : Plot coordinate sections through a selected solution
- [`plot_cv_contours()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/plot_cv_contours.md)
  : Plot CV-surface contours
- [`plot_cv_profiles()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/plot_cv_profiles.md)
  : Plot empirical CV profiles
- [`plot_cv_surface()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/plot_cv_surface.md)
  : Plot the CV surface in 3D
- [`plot_multicrop_curvature()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/plot_multicrop_curvature.md)
  : Plot multi-crop CV contours and experimental-unit criteria
- [`plot_trial_heatmap()`](https://www.elcancu.com/plotsizing/reference/plot_trial_heatmap.md)
  : Plot a yield-grid heatmap
